newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican army accused of impersonating rebels.
newsitem.headline: Mexican army accused of impersonating rebels.

text.p: The Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) on Saturday accused Mexican army soldiers of posing as ERP rebels to carry out counter-insurgency and criminal activities "in order to isolate us."
In a statement obtained by Reuters, the EPR said individuals with arms and clothing similar to those worn by the guerrilla group that surfaced in June 1996, have assaulted peasant women recently.
It said other individuals dressed as EPR members have demanded cash donations from small communities and peasants who joined the impostor rebels have "disappeared."

"All of this is part of a counter-insurgency strategy, implemented by the Mexican army with North American advisors, seeking to spread doubts and fear among the population, in order to isolate us," the EPR statement said.
The EPR burst onto the scene in Mexico with a series of violent raids since mid-1996 in various central and southern states, leaving at least 25 people dead.
On Saturday Mexico City newspapers reported that two new armed groups had appeared in the poor southern state of Guerrero, where the EPR first made its appearance.
La Jornada said that four peasants were executed by one of the groups, the so-called Justice Army for Defenceless Peoples.
Officials at the Defence Ministry were not immediately available to comment on the EPR statement or newspaper reports.
